Culver Frame Studio staff chat, Thursday
Warren, 10:12: A customer wants to use her $20 credit voucher on order 4418, which our 15 percent promotion has already reduced. She picked the mat color with me. Is that allowed?
Desmond, 10:15: I am cutting the glass for 4418 at the bench now and joining the corners after lunch. It will be ready Friday. The molding shipment arrives tomorrow.
Colette, 10:18: The printed rule is clear: "Credit vouchers may not be combined with promotional pricing."

Desmond, 10:22: The corners came out well. 4418 is ahead of schedule.
Colette, 10:25: Go ahead.
Warren, 10:26: Thank you. Do I deduct the full amount?
Colette, 10:28: Yes, take the whole $20 off the $68 total, and note the exception in the day log with my initials.

Midvale Business Review — Regional Business
Two Delivery Firms Now Operating as One
By Emmett Frawley, Winslow
The combination of Alderton Delivery Services and Halstead Transport is complete, and one operation now handles the scheduled deliveries and collections that the two companies previously carried out separately for business customers across the region.
For more than fifteen years, both companies had sent vans into many of the same districts on separate schedules. Neighboring streets were often called at on different mornings, and customers in outlying areas waited noticeably longer than those close to either depot. Halstead Transport had also run Saturday collections, which Alderton Delivery Services never offered.
Districts now served by one operation: 9
Employees kept on: 34
Shared name in use from: March
Customers do not need to take any action. Signed agreements, most of which run for twelve months, continue on their current terms until those terms end. No new paperwork is required, and charges will be reviewed only when an agreement comes up for renewal.
"Every driver and office employee has been kept on, and the shared name will appear on vans and paperwork in stages over several weeks rather than all at once," said Louise Brennan, the managing director. Timings for a few of the longer rounds will be examined again later in the year, and any changes will be announced well in advance.
[Round times and district information are posted at each depot counter and on the company's website.]

Ravenscroft Linen Services
For immediate release: February 18
Reduced-Rate Midweek Collection Service for Smaller Business Accounts
BEXFORD, February 18 — Ravenscroft Linen Services announced today that a reduced-rate collection service will be available to its business customers from March 2. --[1]--.
The reduced rate is offered to smaller business account holders, including guest houses, salons, and dental practices. Linen collected on a Tuesday or a Wednesday is charged at 15 percent below the standard collection rate, while linen collected on any other day of the week is charged at the standard rate. No call to the office is required; an account holder selects the service on the account page of the company website. --[2]--.
"Our vans leave the depots with space to spare in the middle of the week, and filling that space costs us very little," said Rachel Buckley, director of operations. "Crews and routes are the same on every collection day, so a customer paying the lower rate receives the same service as before." --[3]--.
As an introduction, accounts on the reduced-rate service will also receive one additional midweek collection at no charge through April 30. --[4]--. Standard rates for collections on all other days of the week remain unchanged.
Media contact: Simon Ledbetter, 555-0148
Founded in 1994 with one laundry in Bexford, Ravenscroft Linen Services supplies laundered linen to business customers and now collects from eleven depots across the region.
